claim: scMultiome analysis was applied to zebrafish to molecularly resolve all rhombomeres for the first time.
source: Here, we apply scMultiome analysis in zebrafish to molecularly resolve all rhombomeres for the first time.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Rhombomeres become molecularly distinct between 10hpf (end of gastrulation) and 13hpf (early segmentation).
source: We find that rhombomeres become molecularly distinct between 10hpf (end of gastrulation) and 13hpf (early segmentation).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by scMultiome data analysis at different timepoints.

claim: The embryonic hindbrain transiently contains alternating odd- versus even-type rhombomeres.
source: While the embryonic hindbrain transiently contains alternating odd- versus even-type rhombomeres, our scMultiome analyses do not detect extensive odd versus even molecular characteristics in the early hindbrain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is based on established knowledge about hindbrain development.

claim: scMultiome analyses do not detect extensive odd versus even molecular characteristics in the early hindbrain.
source: While the embryonic hindbrain transiently contains alternating odd- versus even-type rhombomeres, our scMultiome analyses do not detect extensive odd versus even molecular characteristics in the early hindbrain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by gene expression and chromatin accessibility analysis.

claim: Each rhombomere displays a unique gene expression and chromatin profile.
source: Instead, we find that each rhombomere displays a unique gene expression and chromatin profile.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by scMultiome data showing distinct molecular profiles for each rhombomere.

claim: Three hindbrain progenitor clusters (PHPDs) were detected prior to the appearance of distinct rhombomeres.
source: Prior to the appearance of distinct rhombomeres, we detect three hindbrain progenitor clusters (PHPDs) that correlate with the earliest visually observed segments in the hindbrain primordium that represent prospective rhombomere r2/r3 (possibly including r1), r4, and r5/r6, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by 10hpf scMultiome data analysis.

claim: The PHPDs correlate with the earliest visually observed segments in the hindbrain primordium representing prospective rhombomere r2/r3 (possibly including r1), r4, and r5/r6.
source: Prior to the appearance of distinct rhombomeres, we detect three hindbrain progenitor clusters (PHPDs) that correlate with the earliest visually observed segments in the hindbrain primordium that represent prospective rhombomere r2/r3 (possibly including r1), r4, and r5/r6, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by comparison of scMultiome data with known developmental patterns.

claim: The PHPDs form in response to Fgf and RA morphogens.
source: We further find that the PHPDs form in response to Fgf and RA morphogens and that individual PHPD cells co-express markers of multiple mature rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by drug treatment experiments with DEAB and SU5402.

claim: Individual PHPD cells co-express markers of multiple mature rhombomeres.
source: We further find that the PHPDs form in response to Fgf and RA morphogens and that individual PHPD cells co-express markers of multiple mature rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by single-cell gene expression analysis and HCR validation.

claim: The PHPDs contain mixed-identity progenitors.
source: We propose that the PHPDs contain mixed-identity progenitors and that their subdivision into individual rhombomeres requires the resolution of mixed transcription and chromatin states.
evidence: This is proposed in the abstract based on the observation of co-expression of multiple rhombomere markers in PHPD cells.

claim: Subdivision of PHPDs into individual rhombomeres requires the resolution of mixed transcription and chromatin states.
source: We propose that the PHPDs contain mixed-identity progenitors and that their subdivision into individual rhombomeres requires the resolution of mixed transcription and chromatin states.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the observed transition from mixed-identity progenitors to distinct rhombomeres.

claim: The embryonic hindbrain is clearly divided into neuromeric units known as rhombomeres.
source: While it remains under debate whether this model applies to the embryonic fore and midbrain, the embryonic hindbrain is clearly divided into neuromeric units known as rhombomeres (Lumsden, 1990), but the unique characteristics of each rhombomere have not been defined molecularly and it remains unclear how they form during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: The unique characteristics of each rhombomere have not been defined molecularly.
source: While it remains under debate whether this model applies to the embryonic fore and midbrain, the embryonic hindbrain is clearly divided into neuromeric units known as rhombomeres (Lumsden, 1990), but the unique characteristics of each rhombomere have not been defined molecularly and it remains unclear how they form during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The hindbrain possesses a two-rhombomere periodicity where each rhombomere pair provides neural crest cells and motor innervation to one specific pharyngeal arch.
source: It has long been noted that the hindbrain possesses a two-rhombomere periodicity where each rhombomere pair provides neural crest cells and motor innervation to one specific pharyngeal arch (Lumsden and Keynes, 1989; Lumsden et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Neuronal differentiation generally occurs earlier in even-numbered rhombomeres.
source: Each pair consists of one odd- and one even-numbered rhombomere that display unique properties – e.g., neuronal differentiation generally occurs earlier in the even-numbered rhombomere.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an example of odd versus even rhombomere differences.

claim: Cells from odd versus even rhombomeres do not intermix but form discrete boundaries when they come into contact.
source: Transplantation experiments further revealed that cells from odd versus even rhombomeres do not intermix but form discrete boundaries when they come into contact (Guthrie and Lumsden, 1991).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior transplantation experiments.

claim: Cells from the even-numbered member of one pair intermix more readily into other even-numbered rhombomeres than into the odd-numbered member of the same pair.
source: Strikingly, cells from the even-numbered member of one pair intermix more readily into other even-numbered rhombomeres than into the odd-numbered member of the same pair (Guthrie et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: egfl6 is expressed in even-numbered rhombomeres.
source: For instance, egfl6 is expressed in even-numbered rhombomeres (Thisse et al., 2001; Choe et al., 2011; Ghosh et al., 2018) and epha4 in odd-numbered ones (Xu et al., 1995), while mafba is expressed in a two-rhombomere unit (r5/r6).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: epha4 is expressed in odd-numbered rhombomeres.
source: For instance, egfl6 is expressed in even-numbered rhombomeres (Thisse et al., 2001; Choe et al., 2011; Ghosh et al., 2018) and epha4 in odd-numbered ones (Xu et al., 1995), while mafba is expressed in a two-rhombomere unit (r5/r6).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: mafba is expressed in a two-rhombomere unit (r5/r6).
source: For instance, egfl6 is expressed in even-numbered rhombomeres (Thisse et al., 2001; Choe et al., 2011; Ghosh et al., 2018) and epha4 in odd-numbered ones (Xu et al., 1995), while mafba is expressed in a two-rhombomere unit (r5/r6).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an example of gene expression patterns.

claim: r5 and r6 can be assigned to the same rhombomere pair by their shared expression of mafba.
source: r5 and r6 can, therefore, be assigned to the same rhombomere pair by their shared expression of mafba and to an even (egfl6 expression in r6) versus odd (epha4 expression in r5) identity, but similar assignments have not been possible for other rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an example of how rhombomere identities can be assigned.

claim: r6 has an even identity based on egfl6 expression.
source: r5 and r6 can, therefore, be assigned to the same rhombomere pair by their shared expression of mafba and to an even (egfl6 expression in r6) versus odd (epha4 expression in r5) identity, but similar assignments have not been possible for other rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an example of rhombomere identity assignment.

claim: r5 has an odd identity based on epha4 expression.
source: r5 and r6 can, therefore, be assigned to the same rhombomere pair by their shared expression of mafba and to an even (egfl6 expression in r6) versus odd (epha4 expression in r5) identity, but similar assignments have not been possible for other rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an example of rhombomere identity assignment.

claim: Relatively few genes have been identified that recapitulate the odd versus even periodicity.
source: Indeed, relatively few genes have been identified that recapitulate this periodicity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of current knowledge.

claim: 'Pro-rhombomeres' have been observed in the chick.
source: For instance, 'pro-rhombomeres' have been observed in the chick (Vaage, 1969) and 'primary' rhombomeres have been proposed in the human (Müller and O'Rahilly, 1997; Müller and O'Rahilly, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: 'Primary' rhombomeres have been proposed in the human.
source: For instance, 'pro-rhombomeres' have been observed in the chick (Vaage, 1969) and 'primary' rhombomeres have been proposed in the human (Müller and O'Rahilly, 1997; Müller and O'Rahilly, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: In zebrafish, the r3/4 and r4/r5 boundaries form first, thereby delineating r4.
source: In the zebrafish, the r3/4 and r4/r5 boundaries form first – thereby delineating r4 – followed by the r6/7 and r1/r2 boundaries that demarcate the r2/r3 and r5/r6 segments.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a description of zebrafish hindbrain development.

claim: The r6/7 and r1/r2 boundaries form after the r3/4 and r4/r5 boundaries, demarcating the r2/r3 and r5/r6 segments.
source: In the zebrafish, the r3/4 and r4/r5 boundaries form first – thereby delineating r4 – followed by the r6/7 and r1/r2 boundaries that demarcate the r2/r3 and r5/r6 segments.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a description of zebrafish hindbrain development.

claim: Zebrafish valentino (val) embryos carry a mutation in the mafba gene that is expressed in r5 and r6.
source: Zebrafish valentino (val) embryos carry a mutation in the mafba gene that is expressed in r5 and r6 (Moens et al., 1998; Moens et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: In val animals, r5 and r6 do not form, but are replaced by an 'rX' segment that displays mixed r5/r6 identity.
source: In val animals, r5 and r6 do not form, but are replaced by an 'rX' segment that displays mixed r5/r6 identity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to prior work on valentino mutants.

claim: rX was interpreted to represent an early 'protosegment' containing progenitors for r5 and r6.
source: This finding was interpreted to mean that rX represents an early 'protosegment' containing progenitors for r5 and r6, but it is unclear if rX cells exist in wild-type embryos and there is no genetic or molecular evidence suggesting the presence of equivalent progenitor domains for other rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an interpretation of prior findings.

claim: It is unclear if rX cells exist in wild-type embryos.
source: This finding was interpreted to mean that rX represents an early 'protosegment' containing progenitors for r5 and r6, but it is unclear if rX cells exist in wild-type embryos and there is no genetic or molecular evidence suggesting the presence of equivalent progenitor domains for other rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge.

claim: There is no genetic or molecular evidence suggesting the presence of equivalent progenitor domains for other rhombomeres.
source: This finding was interpreted to mean that rX represents an early 'protosegment' containing progenitors for r5 and r6, but it is unclear if rX cells exist in wild-type embryos and there is no genetic or molecular evidence suggesting the presence of equivalent progenitor domains for other rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Recent scRNAseq analyses could not fully resolve individual rhombomeres.
source: Attempts at better defining rhombomere identities and understanding their formation have been hampered by a lack of comprehensive molecular data, as recent scRNAseq analyses could not fully resolve individual rhombomeres (Jiang et al., 2021; Farnsworth et al., 2020; Wagner et al., 2018; Tambalo et al., 2020; Farrell et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Individual rhombomeres are readily identifiable in the 13hpf neural UMAP based on their gene expression profiles.
source: At early segmentation stages (13hpf), individual rhombomeres are readily identifiable in the neural UMAP based on their gene expression profiles.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the UMAP analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: The r3, r5, and r6 clusters are immediately recognizable based on the known expression of egr2b (restricted to r3 and r5), mafba (restricted to r5 and r6), and sema3ab (restricted to r5 at this stage).
source: The r3, r5, and r6 clusters are immediately recognizable based on the known expression of egr2b (restricted to r3 and r5; Figure 1E; Oxtoby and Jowett, 1993), mafba (restricted to r5 and r6; Figure 1F; Moens et al., 1998), and sema3ab (restricted to r5 at this stage; Figure 1G; Roos et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 1 and citations to prior work.

claim: r4 forms a distinct cluster that is characterized by expression of fgf3 (enriched in r4) and cyp26b1 that is expressed in r4 before gradually expanding to r3.
source: r4 forms a distinct cluster that is characterized by expression of fgf3 (enriched in r4; Figure 1H; Walshe and Mason, 2003), as well as cyp26b1 that is expressed in r4 before gradually expanding to r3 (Figure 1I; Zhao et al., 2005) – which we confirmed by hybridization chain reaction (HCR) analysis (Figure 1Q).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 1 and citations to prior work, plus HCR validation.

claim: tgfbr2b and vgll3 are highly enriched in the r2 cluster.
source: Our data reveal that tgfbr2b and vgll3 are highly enriched in this cluster (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1.

claim: vgll3 is restricted to r2 in 13hpf zebrafish embryos.
source: We, therefore, examined vgll3 expression in 13hpf zebrafish embryos and find that it is restricted to r2, confirming the identity of this cluster (Figure 1R).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1R showing HCR validation.

claim: A cluster found next to r2 is enriched for irx1b and corresponds to r1.
source: A cluster found next to r2 is enriched for irx1b (Figure 1L) and our HCR analysis detected irx1b immediately anterior to vgll3 expression (Figure 1S), indicating that this cluster corresponds to r1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 1 showing gene expression and HCR validation.

claim: Dorsal (casz1 and zic2a) and ventral (ntn1a and sp8b) genes are differentially expressed across each rhombomere at 13hpf.
source: A closer examination revealed that dorsal (casz1 and zic2a; Grinblat and Sive, 2001) and ventral (ntn1a and sp8b; Lauderdale et al., 1997; Kawakami et al., 2004) genes are differentially expressed across each rhombomere at 13hpf (Figure 1M–P), indicating that dorsoventral (DV) patterning is ongoing at this stage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 1 and citations to prior work.

claim: Dorsoventral (DV) patterning is ongoing at 13hpf.
source: A closer examination revealed that dorsal (casz1 and zic2a; Grinblat and Sive, 2001) and ventral (ntn1a and sp8b; Lauderdale et al., 1997; Kawakami et al., 2004) genes are differentially expressed across each rhombomere at 13hpf (Figure 1M–P), indicating that dorsoventral (DV) patterning is ongoing at this stage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the differential expression of DV markers.

claim: At 13hpf and 16hpf, the r3 and r5 clusters display a strong enrichment for accessible EGR2 motifs.
source: At both 13hpf and 16hpf, the r3 and r5 clusters display a strong enrichment for accessible EGR2 motifs (Figure 4C; consistent with high expression of egr2b in both rhombomeres), but the r3 and r5 clusters also differ from each other such that the r5 cluster is enriched for accessible MAF motifs (Figure 4D; in agreement with mafba expression in r5) and r3 is enriched in accessible binding motifs for TALE TFs (such as PKNOX1 [a.k.a., Prep1]; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 showing motif enrichment analysis.

claim: The r5 cluster is enriched for accessible MAF motifs.
source: At both 13hpf and 16hpf, the r3 and r5 clusters display a strong enrichment for accessible EGR2 motifs (Figure 4C; consistent with high expression of egr2b in both rhombomeres), but the r3 and r5 clusters also differ from each other such that the r5 cluster is enriched for accessible MAF motifs (Figure 4D; in agreement with mafba expression in r5) and r3 is enriched in accessible binding motifs for TALE TFs (such as PKNOX1 [a.k.a., Prep1]; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 showing motif enrichment analysis.

claim: r3 is enriched in accessible binding motifs for TALE TFs (such as PKNOX1).
source: At both 13hpf and 16hpf, the r3 and r5 clusters display a strong enrichment for accessible EGR2 motifs (Figure 4C; consistent with high expression of egr2b in both rhombomeres), but the r3 and r5 clusters also differ from each other such that the r5 cluster is enriched for accessible MAF motifs (Figure 4D; in agreement with mafba expression in r5) and r3 is enriched in accessible binding motifs for TALE TFs (such as PKNOX1 [a.k.a., Prep1]; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 showing motif enrichment analysis.

claim: r6 shows enrichment for accessible MAF motifs and PG4 HOX motifs.
source: r6 shows enrichment for accessible MAF motifs (Figure 4D; in accordance with mafba expression in r6), as well as for paralog group (PG) 4 HOX motifs (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 showing motif enrichment analysis.

claim: The r4 cluster is enriched for Pbx binding motifs that are also accessible in some more caudal tissues.
source: The r4 cluster is enriched for Pbx binding motifs that are also accessible in some more caudal tissues (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 showing motif enrichment analysis.

claim: Cells in the r2 cluster are highly enriched for accessible binding motifs for TEAD family TFs at 13hpf.
source: Cells in the r2 cluster are highly enriched for accessible binding motifs for TEAD family TFs at 13hpf (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 showing motif enrichment analysis.

claim: TEAD TFs are known heterodimerization partners to Vgll TFs.
source: TEAD TF expression is not restricted to r2 (Figure 4A and B), but TEAD TFs are known heterodimerization partners to Vgll TFs (Günther et al., 2004; Maeda et al., 2002) and vgll3 expression is restricted to r2 (Figure 1J and R–T).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: Vgll3 supports the binding of TEAD TFs to genomic DNA specifically in r2.
source: This suggests that Vgll3 supports the binding of TEAD TFs to genomic DNA specifically in r2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the co-expression of vgll3 and TEAD motif enrichment in r2.

claim: The r1 and r2 clusters (along with some MHB clusters) display enrichment for NR2C/F family motifs.
source: We did not identify any TF binding motifs unique to r1, but the r1 and r2 clusters (along with some MHB clusters) display enrichment for NR2C/F family motifs (Figure 4I and J), consistent with nr2f1b being expressed in this region of the zebrafish embryo (Love and Prince, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 and citation to prior work.

claim: r1-r6 are molecularly distinct from each other and adjacent neural structures by 13hpf.
source: Overall, we find strong agreement between the scRNA and scATAC data in defining individual rhombomeres and we conclude that r1-r6 are molecularly distinct from each other and adjacent neural structures by 13hpf, which precedes the stage when individual rhombomeres become visually detectable in zebrafish.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the scMultiome analysis.

claim: 13hpf precedes the stage when individual rhombomeres become visually detectable in zebrafish.
source: Overall, we find strong agreement between the scRNA and scATAC data in defining individual rhombomeres and we conclude that r1-r6 are molecularly distinct from each other and adjacent neural structures by 13hpf, which precedes the stage when individual rhombomeres become visually detectable in zebrafish.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a temporal comparison.

claim: The UMAPs do not show odd and even rhombomeres clustering into separate groups.
source: The UMAPs presented in Figures 1 and 2 do not show odd and even rhombomeres clustering into separate groups.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figures 1 and 2.

claim: r1, r2, and r4 cluster with anterior neural structures, while r6 clusters closer to caudal structures.
source: Instead, r1, r2, and r4 cluster with anterior neural structures, while r6 clusters closer to caudal structures.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the UMAP analysis.

claim: The heatmaps reveal considerable gene expression overlap between r3 and r5.
source: The heatmaps reveal considerable gene expression overlap between r3 and r5, but these rhombomeres do not share extensive expression with r1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A and B.

claim: r3 and r5 do not share extensive expression with r1.
source: The heatmaps reveal considerable gene expression overlap between r3 and r5, but these rhombomeres do not share extensive expression with r1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A and B.

claim: r2, r4, and r6 share some gene expression, but r2 seems to express more genes related to r3, and r6 shares closer expression with r5.
source: Similarly, while r2, r4, and r6 share some gene expression, r2 seems to express more genes related to r3, and r6 shares closer expression with r5.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the heatmap analysis.

claim: At both 13hpf and 16hpf, r3 and r5 are closely related to each other.
source: This analysis revealed very similar relationships at 13hpf and 16hpf. At both stages, r3 and r5 are closely related to each other, while r1 is more closely related to the MHB (13hpf) or r2 (16hpf).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5C and D showing dendrograms.

claim: r1 is more closely related to the MHB at 13hpf or r2 at 16hpf.
source: This analysis revealed very similar relationships at 13hpf and 16hpf. At both stages, r3 and r5 are closely related to each other, while r1 is more closely related to the MHB (13hpf) or r2 (16hpf).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5C and D showing dendrograms.

claim: r4 is related to r2, but not to r6.
source: Furthermore, r4 is related to r2, but not to r6, which instead clusters with the caudal hindbrain at both stages.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the dendrogram analysis.

claim: r6 clusters with the caudal hindbrain at both 13hpf and 16hpf.
source: Furthermore, r4 is related to r2, but not to r6, which instead clusters with the caudal hindbrain at both stages.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the dendrogram analysis.

claim: There is no clustering of even versus odd rhombomeres at either 13hpf or 16hpf.
source: As a result, there is no clustering of even versus odd rhombomeres at either 13hpf or 16hpf.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the dendrogram analysis.

claim: Very few genes fulfill the criteria of being expressed in r2, r4, and r6 with average expression exceeding their expression in r1, r3, and r5, or vice versa at 13hpf.
source: To more directly assess if there is a molecular odd versus even pattern among rhombomeres, we computationally identified any genes expressed in r2, r4, and r6 – and whose average expression in those rhombomeres exceeds their expression in r1, r3, and r5 – or vice versa at 13hpf (Figure 5E and F). We find very few genes that fulfill these criteria.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5E and F.

claim: col7a1l is highly expressed in r2, r4, and r6.
source: col7a1l is highly expressed in r2, r4, and r6, but most other genes expressed in an even or odd patterns are expressed weakly in one of the rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an example of a gene with even rhombomere expression.

claim: plxna2 is robustly expressed in r2 and r4, but only weakly in r6.
source: For instance, plxna2 is robustly expressed in r2 and r4, but only weakly in r6, while egr2b, epha4a, and sema3fb are highly expressed in r3 and r5, but barely detectable in r1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an example of a gene with partial even rhombomere expression.

claim: egr2b, epha4a, and sema3fb are highly expressed in r3 and r5, but barely detectable in r1.
source: For instance, plxna2 is robustly expressed in r2 and r4, but only weakly in r6, while egr2b, epha4a, and sema3fb are highly expressed in r3 and r5, but barely detectable in r1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an example of genes with partial odd rhombomere expression.

claim: Several genes are co-expressed in r5 and r6, like mafba and the PG3 and PG4 hox genes.
source: This analysis identified several genes co-expressed in r5 and r6 (Figure 5I), like the known expression of mafba (Moens et al., 1998) and the PG3 and PG4 hox genes (Prince et al., 1998a; Prince et al., 1998b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5I and citations to prior work.

claim: Only a few genes are co-expressed in r1 and r2 (nrp2a and pdzrn4).
source: In contrast, we detect only a few genes co-expressed in r1 and r2 (nrp2a and pdzrn4; Figure 5G) and none co-expressed in r3 and r4.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5G.

claim: No genes are co-expressed in r3 and r4.
source: In contrast, we detect only a few genes co-expressed in r1 and r2 (nrp2a and pdzrn4; Figure 5G) and none co-expressed in r3 and r4.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the gene co-expression analysis.

claim: Each rhombomere is characterized by a unique GRN with previously known, as well as novel, TFs acting as nodes.
source: This analysis revealed that each rhombomere is characterized by a unique GRN with previously known, as well as novel, TFs acting as nodes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the GRN analysis.

claim: The TEAD1 TF forms a predominant node in r2.
source: For example, the TEAD1 TF forms a predominant node in r2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), as expected based on its known interaction with Vgll3 that is uniquely expressed in r2, but so do the Sox6 and Esrrg TFs that have not been previously implicated in r2 formation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Sox6 and Esrrg TFs form nodes in the r2 GRN but have not been previously implicated in r2 formation.
source: For example, the TEAD1 TF forms a predominant node in r2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), as expected based on its known interaction with Vgll3 that is uniquely expressed in r2, but so do the Sox6 and Esrrg TFs that have not been previously implicated in r2 formation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a novel finding from the GRN analysis.

claim: Nr2f family TFs form nodes in both the r1 and r2 GRNs.
source: While some TFs are shared between rhombomeres, such as Nr2f family TFs forming nodes in both the r1 and r2 GRNs (Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2), the GRNs are clearly distinct.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: r3 and r5 both have a predominant Egr2 node in their GRNs.
source: Even when comparing rhombomeres that share significant molecular similarity – such as r3 and r5 that both have a predominant Egr2 node – we find that their GRNs also possess numerous distinct nodes – such as the PG 3 and 4 hox genes in r5 but not r3 (Figure 5—figure supplements 3 and 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplements 3 and 5.

claim: The r5 GRN possesses PG 3 and 4 hox genes as nodes, but r3 does not.
source: Even when comparing rhombomeres that share significant molecular similarity – such as r3 and r5 that both have a predominant Egr2 node – we find that their GRNs also possess numerous distinct nodes – such as the PG 3 and 4 hox genes in r5 but not r3 (Figure 5—figure supplements 3 and 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplements 3 and 5.

claim: TFs that are shared between rhombomeres are connected to different genes in each GRN.
source: Lastly, even TFs that are shared between rhombomeres are connected to different genes in each GRN, as illustrated by Egr2 connecting to MafB and RARa in r5, but not r3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 7.

claim: Each 13hpf rhombomere is characterized by a unique GRN that defines a specific molecular identity.
source: We conclude that each 13hpf rhombomere is characterized by a unique GRN that defines a specific molecular identity, and that there is not an overt molecular odd versus even, or rhombomere pair, pattern at this stage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the GRN analysis.

claim: There is not an overt molecular odd versus even, or rhombomere pair, pattern at 13hpf.
source: We conclude that each 13hpf rhombomere is characterized by a unique GRN that defines a specific molecular identity, and that there is not an overt molecular odd versus even, or rhombomere pair, pattern at this stage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the comprehensive molecular analysis.

claim: Individual rhombomeres are not apparent as distinct clusters at 10hpf.
source: We find that, in contrast to 13hpf and 16hpf, individual rhombomeres are not apparent as distinct clusters at 10hpf.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the 10hpf UMAP analysis.

claim: Three clusters (HB.1-HB.3) were identified at 10hpf that express genes characteristic of mature rhombomeres.
source: Instead, we identified three clusters (HB.1-HB.3) that express genes characteristic of mature rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the 10hpf scMultiome analysis.

claim: HB.1 is the largest cluster and expresses genes associated with several different rhombomeres such that vgll3 (an r2 marker) and egr2b (a marker of r3 and r5) are both enriched in this cluster.
source: HB.1 is the largest of these and expresses genes associated with several different rhombomeres such that vgll3 (Figure 3D; an r2 marker; Figure 1R; Simon et al., 2017) and egr2b (Figure 3E; a marker of r3 and r5; Oxtoby and Jowett, 1993) are both enriched in this cluster.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 3 and citations to prior work.

claim: HB.2 expresses mafba (a marker of r5/r6) and crabp2a (expressed in r6, the caudal hindbrain, and weakly in r4/r5), as well as limited egr2b.
source: A second prominent rhombomere cluster (HB.2) expresses mafba (Figure 3F; a marker of r5/r6; Moens et al., 1998) and crabp2a (Figure 3G; expressed in r6, the caudal hindbrain, and weakly in r4/r5; Sharma et al., 2005), as well as limited egr2b (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 3 and citations to prior work.

claim: egr2b expression is initiated in r3 at the end of gastrulation (10hpf), but does not become expressed in r5 until 11hpf.
source: Since egr2b expression is initiated in r3 at the end of gastrulation (10hpf), but does not become expressed in r5 until 11hpf, this suggests that HB.1 and HB.2 correspond to prospective anterior and posterior rhombomeres, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as temporal information about gene expression.

claim: HB.1 and HB.2 correspond to prospective anterior and posterior rhombomeres, respectively.
source: Since egr2b expression is initiated in r3 at the end of gastrulation (10hpf), but does not become expressed in r5 until 11hpf, this suggests that HB.1 and HB.2 correspond to prospective anterior and posterior rhombomeres, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from gene expression patterns.

claim: HB.3 is related to HB.1 as these two clusters co-express cyp26b1 and cyp26c1 (expressed in r2-r4).
source: Furthermore, a third rhombomere cluster (HB.3) is related to HB.1 as these two clusters co-express cyp26b1 and cyp26c1 (Figure 3H, I; expressed in r2-r4; Zhao et al., 2005; Gu et al., 2005), but HB.3 does not express either vgll3 or egr2b (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 3 and citations to prior work.

claim: HB.3 does not express either vgll3 or egr2b.
source: Furthermore, a third rhombomere cluster (HB.3) is related to HB.1 as these two clusters co-express cyp26b1 and cyp26c1 (Figure 3H, I; expressed in r2-r4; Zhao et al., 2005; Gu et al., 2005), but HB.3 does not express either vgll3 or egr2b (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3.

claim: HB.3 expresses dusp2 and ppp1r14ab, two markers restricted to r4 at 10hpf.
source: Instead, HB.3 expresses dusp2 and ppp1r14ab, two markers that we previously reported as restricted to r4 at this stage (Figure 3J and K; Choe et al., 2011; Maurer and Sagerström, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 3 and citations to prior work.

claim: HB.1 likely corresponds to the future r2/r3 (and possibly r1), HB.2 to r5/r6 and HB.3 to r4.
source: Taken together, this analysis demonstrates that individual rhombomeres are not yet molecularly distinct at 10hpf. Instead, three progenitor domains with different anteroposterior characteristics are present, such that HB.1 likely corresponds to the future r2/r3 (and possibly r1), HB.2 to r5/r6 and HB.3 to r4.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the 10hpf analysis.

claim: Individual HB.1 cells co-express r2 and r3 markers.
source: Examining the expression state of individual HB.1 cells, we identified many cells that express both vgll3 (r2 marker) and egr2b (r3 marker at this stage), such that ~74% of egr2b-expressing cells co-express vgll3 at 10hpf (Figure 6F; top left panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6F showing single-cell co-expression analysis.

claim: ~74% of egr2b-expressing cells co-express vgll3 at 10hpf.
source: Examining the expression state of individual HB.1 cells, we identified many cells that express both vgll3 (r2 marker) and egr2b (r3 marker at this stage), such that ~74% of egr2b-expressing cells co-express vgll3 at 10hpf (Figure 6F; top left panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6F showing quantification of co-expression.

claim: At 13hpf, r2 cells do not co-express egr2b and only ~10% of r3 cells co-express vgll3.
source: This contrasts with 13hpf – when r2 cells do not co-express egr2b and only ~10% of r3 cells co-express vgll3 – and 16hpf, when egr2b is fully restricted to r3 and vgll3 is being downregulated (Figure 6F; top right panels).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6F showing temporal changes in co-expression.

claim: 62% of vgll3 positive HB.1 cells co-express nab1b.
source: In addition to co-expressing egr2b, we find that vgll3-positive HB.1 cells also co-express nab1b (r3 and r5 marker; Mechta-Grigoriou et al., 2000; Figure 1T) such that 62% of vgll3 positive HB.1 cells co-express nab1b (Figure 6F; bottom left panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6F and citation to prior work.

claim: ~72% of vgll3-positive HB.1 cells co-express either egr2b or nab1b.
source: When considered in combination, ~72% of vgll3-positive HB.1 cells co-express either egr2b or nab1b (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1B showing combined co-expression analysis.

claim: Extensive overlap between vgll3 and both egr2b and nab1b expression was found at the earliest stages that these genes can be detected in zebrafish embryos.
source: To identify the HB.1 domain and assess the co-expression of rhombomere markers in vivo, we turned to HCR analysis in zebrafish embryos. We find extensive overlap between vgll3 and both egr2b and nab1b expression at the earliest stages that these genes can be detected (Figure 6G and H), indicating that HB.1 cells possess mixed rhombomere identities in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6G and H showing HCR validation.

claim: HB.1 cells possess mixed rhombomere identities in vivo.
source: To identify the HB.1 domain and assess the co-expression of rhombomere markers in vivo, we turned to HCR analysis in zebrafish embryos. We find extensive overlap between vgll3 and both egr2b and nab1b expression at the earliest stages that these genes can be detected (Figure 6G and H), indicating that HB.1 cells possess mixed rhombomere identities in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the HCR analysis.

claim: The molecular profile of cells in each PHPD at 10hpf differs from that of its derivative rhombomere cells at 13hpf.
source: To begin characterizing the transition from PHPD cells to rhombomere cells, we made use of our time course of scMultiome data. We compared the molecular profile of cells in each PHPD at 10hpf to that of its derivative rhombomere cells at 13hpf and projected as heatmaps (Figure 6I; Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6I and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The PHPDs differ from later rhombomeres in terms of their molecular profile.
source: We conclude that the PHPDs differ from later rhombomeres in terms of their molecular profile and, at least in the case of HB.1, individual PHPD cells possess mixed identities characterized by co-expression of markers for multiple rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the temporal comparison analysis.

claim: Individual PHPD cells possess mixed identities characterized by co-expression of markers for multiple rhombomeres.
source: We conclude that the PHPDs differ from later rhombomeres in terms of their molecular profile and, at least in the case of HB.1, individual PHPD cells possess mixed identities characterized by co-expression of markers for multiple rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the co-expression analysis.

claim: During the development of PHPD cells into rhombomeres, their gene expression profiles undergo a corresponding change.
source: During the development of PHPD cells into rhombomeres, their gene expression profiles undergo a corresponding change.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the temporal analysis.

claim: The anteroposterior pattern of the early hindbrain primordium is established by morphogens, with RA acting posteriorly and Fgfs acting anteriorly.
source: The anteroposterior pattern of the early hindbrain primordium is established by morphogens (reviewed in Krumlauf and Wilkinson, 2021; Frank and Sela-Donenfeld, 2019), with RA acting posteriorly (from its source in the adjacent somites) and Fgfs acting anteriorly (with an initial source at the MHB followed by a secondary source in r4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to review articles.

claim: Expression of RA signaling components (RARab and crabp2a) is enriched in HB.2 cells.
source: Accordingly, we find that expression of RA signaling components – such as the RARab retinoic acid receptor and the crabp2a retinoic acid binding protein – is enriched in HB.2 cells (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7A and B.

claim: egr2b expression in r5 and mafba expression in r5/r6 is detected by 10hpf-11hpf in control embryos but is never observed in DEAB-treated embryos.
source: We find that egr2b expression in r5 and mafba expression in r5/r6 is detected by 10hpf-11hpf in control embryos but is never observed in DEAB-treated embryos (Figure 7H–K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7H–K showing HCR analysis of DEAB-treated embryos.

claim: The expression of anterior markers (vgll3, cyp26b1, cyp26c1, and the anterior egr2b domain) persists in DEAB-treated embryos, but the expression is observed over a broader region and may be somewhat weaker.
source: In contrast, the expression of the anterior markers (vgll3, cyp26b1, cyp26c1, and the anterior egr2b domain) persists in DEAB-treated embryos, but the expression is observed over a broader region and may be somewhat weaker.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from DEAB treatment experiments.

claim: Inhibition of RA signaling does not appear to induce an rX domain, but leads to a loss of the caudal hindbrain and an expansion of r4.
source: To determine if such an rX domain forms in place of r5/r6 in DEAB-treated embryos, we assessed expression of cdx4 in the spinal cord relative to cyp26b1 in r4 and egr2b in r3 (Figure 7L and M). We again observe a slight expansion of egr2b in r3 and cyp26b1a in r4 of DEAB-treated embryos, but these domains closely abut cdx4 expression. Inhibition of RA signaling, therefore, does not appear to induce an rX domain, but leads to a loss of the caudal hindbrain and an expansion of r4, consistent with a role for RA in HB.2 formation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7L and M showing marker gene expression analysis.

claim: Vagal (nX) neurons in the caudal hindbrain and abducens (nVI) neurons in r5/r6 are largely absent in DEAB-treated embryos.
source: We find that vagal (nX) neurons in the caudal hindbrain and abducens (nVI) neurons in r5/r6 are largely absent in DEAB-treated embryos while r4-derived facial (nVII) neurons and r4-specific reticulospinal Mauthner neurons (MNs) appear expanded (2 MNs per wild-type embryo versus 3.6 MNs per DEAB-treated embryo).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from neuronal differentiation analysis.

claim: r4-derived facial (nVII) neurons and r4-specific reticulospinal Mauthner neurons (MNs) appear expanded in DEAB-treated embryos (2 MNs per wild-type embryo versus 3.6 MNs per DEAB-treated embryo).
source: We find that vagal (nX) neurons in the caudal hindbrain and abducens (nVI) neurons in r5/r6 are largely absent in DEAB-treated embryos while r4-derived facial (nVII) neurons and r4-specific reticulospinal Mauthner neurons (MNs) appear expanded (2 MNs per wild-type embryo versus 3.6 MNs per DEAB-treated embryo).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with quantification of neuronal numbers.

claim: Loss of RA signaling leads to loss of the HB.2 domain and to the expansion of the HB.3 domain.
source: We conclude that loss of RA signaling leads to loss of the HB.2 domain and to the expansion of the HB.3 domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the DEAB treatment experiments.

claim: Treatment with SU5402 (an inhibitor of Fgf receptor signaling) blocks expression of vgll3 and egr2b in r2/r3 at 10hpf.
source: In agreement with a role also for Fgf signaling, we detect expression of Fgf8 and Fgf3 in several PHPD clusters of the 10hpf UMAP (Figure 7C and D), and we find that treatment with SU5402 (an inhibitor of Fgf receptor signaling) blocks expression of vgll3 and egr2b in r2/r3 at 10hpf (Figure 7N) – as well as of mafba and egr2b in r5/r6 and of hoxb1a in r4 – when those genes first become detectable at 12hpf-13hpf (Figure 7O and P).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7N showing HCR analysis of SU5402-treated embryos.

claim: SU5402 treatment blocks expression of mafba and egr2b in r5/r6 and of hoxb1a in r4 when those genes first become detectable at 12hpf-13hpf.
source: In agreement with a role also for Fgf signaling, we detect expression of Fgf8 and Fgf3 in several PHPD clusters of the 10hpf UMAP (Figure 7C and D), and we find that treatment with SU5402 (an inhibitor of Fgf receptor signaling) blocks expression of vgll3 and egr2b in r2/r3 at 10hpf (Figure 7N) – as well as of mafba and egr2b in r5/r6 and of hoxb1a in r4 – when those genes first become detectable at 12hpf-13hpf (Figure 7O and P).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7O and P showing HCR analysis of SU5402-treated embryos.

claim: While RA is required for HB.2 formation, Fgf appears broadly required to establish the PHPDs.
source: Therefore, while RA is required for HB.2 formation, Fgf appears broadly required to establish the PHPDs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the morphogen inhibition experiments.

claim: The r5 and r6 clusters contain only cells from control embryos and no cells from DEAB-treated embryos.
source: In assessing the contribution of control versus DEAB-treated cells to each UMAP cluster, we find that the r5 and r6 clusters contain only cells from control embryos and no cells from DEAB-treated embryos (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7F showing integrated UMAP analysis.

claim: Projecting DEAB-treated and wild-type samples in separate UMAPs reveals a complete loss of r5 and r6 in the DEAB condition.
source: Accordingly, projecting DEAB-treated and wild-type samples in separate UMAPs reveals a complete loss of r5 and r6 in the DEAB condition (Figure 7G), consistent with the HB.2 progenitor population not forming.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7G showing separate UMAPs.

claim: r1 and r2 contain twice as many cells, and r4 contains almost three times as many cells, in DEAB-treated compared to control embryos.
source: In agreement with the apparent expansion of anterior rhombomeres observed in our HCR analyses of DEAB-treated embryos, cell ratio comparisons reveal that r1 and r2 contain twice as many cells, and r4 contains almost three times as many cells, in DEAB-treated compared to control embryos (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7F showing cell ratio comparisons.

claim: The caudal hindbrain (CHB) clusters are lost in DEAB-treated embryos while the spinal cord clusters largely persist.
source: Furthermore, the caudal hindbrain (CHB) clusters are lost in DEAB-treated embryos while the spinal cord clusters largely persist (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7F and G.

claim: All cells from DEAB-treated embryos can be mapped to a wild-type cluster, indicating that an rX domain does not form in DEAB-treated embryos.
source: We also find that all cells from DEAB-treated embryos can be mapped to a wild-type cluster, again indicating that an rX domain does not form in DEAB-treated embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the integrated UMAP analysis.

claim: Only ~30 genes are differentially expressed between DEAB-treated and control embryos (>twofold change; p-val <1e-5) in each rhombomere.
source: Furthermore, we find only minor changes in gene expression in r1-r4 upon loss of RA signaling (Figure 7—figure supplement 2; Figure 7—source data 1). Only ~30 genes are differentially expressed between DEAB-treated and control embryos (>twofold change; p-val <1e-5) in each rhombomere – and many of these genes are shared between rhombomeres – indicating that they reflect broadly RA-responsive genes rather than genes that affect individual rhombomere fates.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 2 showing differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Many differentially expressed genes between DEAB-treated and control embryos are shared between rhombomeres, indicating that they reflect broadly RA-responsive genes rather than genes that affect individual rhombomere fates.
source: Furthermore, we find only minor changes in gene expression in r1-r4 upon loss of RA signaling (Figure 7—figure supplement 2; Figure 7—source data 1). Only ~30 genes are differentially expressed between DEAB-treated and control embryos (>twofold change; p-val <1e-5) in each rhombomere – and many of these genes are shared between rhombomeres – indicating that they reflect broadly RA-responsive genes rather than genes that affect individual rhombomere fates.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the differential gene expression analysis.

claim: RA is required for formation of the HB.2, but not the HB.1 or HB.3 domains.
source: Our results suggest that RA is required for formation of the HB.2, but not the HB.1 or HB.3 domains, although we cannot exclude the possibility that a small number of genes are RA-dependent in the anterior domains.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the DEAB treatment experiments.

claim: Using combined single nucleus RNAseq and ATACseq (scMultiome), all rhombomeres were successfully resolved at zebrafish segmentation stages.
source: Using combined single nucleus RNAseq and ATACseq (scMultiome), we successfully resolved all rhombomeres at zebrafish segmentation stages.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the main finding.

claim: A unique molecular profile was identified for each rhombomere.
source: We identify a unique molecular profile for each rhombomere and find that there is no overt odd versus even periodicity of rhombomere identities at these stages.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the main finding.

claim: Three mixed-identity progenitor domains were defined that likely correspond to the pre-rhombomeres observed visually in early embryos of several species.
source: We also define three mixed-identity progenitor domains that likely correspond to the pre-rhombomeres observed visually in early embryos of several species and that are predicted to subsequently subdivide into the mature rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the main finding.

claim: Using the full gene expression profile for each rhombomere at segmentation stages, r3 and r5 are closely related and r2 shares features with r4, but r1 and r6 do not fall into these groups.
source: Using the full gene expression profile for each rhombomere at segmentation stages, we find that r3 and r5 are closely related and that r2 shares features with r4, but r1 and r6 do not fall into these groups (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 5.

claim: The GRNs of individual rhombomeres are unique – even closely related rhombomeres (e.g. r3 and r5) have clearly distinct GRNs.
source: The GRNs of individual rhombomeres are unique – even closely related rhombomeres (e.g. r3 and r5) have clearly distinct GRNs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the GRN analysis.

claim: Analyses of gene expression, TF motif accessibility, and GRN formation combine to indicate that repeating two-segment identities are not molecularly evident in the early zebrafish hindbrain.
source: Our analyses of gene expression, TF motif accessibility, and GRN formation combine to indicate that repeating two-segment identities are not molecularly evident in the early zebrafish hindbrain.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the comprehensive molecular analysis.

claim: If cell surface receptors are expressed in an even versus odd pattern to drive cell sorting, the shared expression modules may be a minor component of the overall GRN in each rhombomere.
source: If cell surface receptors are expressed in an even versus odd pattern to drive cell sorting, why do we not detect a corresponding molecular periodicity? The answer may be that these shared expression modules are a minor component of the overall GRN in each rhombomere.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed explanation for the lack of molecular periodicity.

claim: Prior work revealed a hierarchy for cell mixing such that r3 cells mix more readily with other r3 cells than with cells from different odd-numbered rhombomeres.
source: Indeed, prior work also revealed a hierarchy for cell mixing such that, for instance, r3 cells mix more readily with other r3 cells than with cells from different odd-numbered rhombomeres (Guthrie et al., 1993) – indicating that the GRNs controlling expression of cell surface receptors may not be the same in all odd rhombomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior work.

claim: epha7 is part of the Egr2 regulatory network in both r3 and r5.
source: Accordingly, we find that epha7 is part of the Egr2 regulatory network in both r3 and r5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 7.

claim: epha2 is part of the Egr2 network in r5, but not in r3.
source: In agreement, we find that epha2 is part of the Egr2 network in r5, but not in r3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 7.

claim: When comparing the Egr2 regulatory network in r3 versus r5, only 37% of nodes are shared.
source: In fact, if we compare the Egr2 regulatory network in r3 versus r5 (the two most closely related rhombomeres where Egr2 is an essential TF), we find that only 37% of nodes are shared.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a quantification of GRN similarity.

claim: A transient r2 + r3 structure is formed before being subdivided by the formation of the r2/r3 boundary.
source: This is followed by the r1/r2 boundary, which leaves a transient r2 + r3 structure that is subsequently subdivided by the formation of the r2/r3 boundary.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of zebrafish hindbrain development.

claim: A transient r5 + r6 segment is formed before being subdivided by the r5/r6 boundary.
source: Similarly, a transient r5 + r6 segment is formed before being subdivided by the r5/r6 boundary (Moens et al., 1998; Moens and Prince, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior work.

claim: Three 'pre-rhombomeres' have been observed in chick.
source: The formation of early transient segments may be evolutionarily conserved, since three potentially analogous 'pre-rhombomeres' have been observed in chick and four 'primary rhombomeres' (where the fourth corresponds to the caudal hindbrain) are present in human embryos (Vaage, 1969; Müller and O'Rahilly, 1997; Müller and O'Rahilly, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior work.

claim: Four 'primary rhombomeres' (where the fourth corresponds to the caudal hindbrain) are present in human embryos.
source: The formation of early transient segments may be evolutionarily conserved, since three potentially analogous 'pre-rhombomeres' have been observed in chick and four 'primary rhombomeres' (where the fourth corresponds to the caudal hindbrain) are present in human embryos (Vaage, 1969; Müller and O'Rahilly, 1997; Müller and O'Rahilly, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior work.

claim: The 10hpf Multiome data identify three hindbrain populations (PHPDs), and analyses demonstrate that they contain rhombomere progenitors.
source: Our 10hpf Multiome data identify three hindbrain populations (PHPDs), and our analyses demonstrate that they contain rhombomere progenitors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the main finding.

claim: The HB.2 population contains r5 + r6 progenitors, suggesting that it corresponds to rX.
source: The HB.2 population contains r5 + r6 progenitors, suggesting that it corresponds to rX, while HB.3 appears to correspond to the r4 segment, and HB.1 to the r2 + r3 segment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the PHPD analysis.

claim: HB.3 appears to correspond to the r4 segment.
source: The HB.2 population contains r5 + r6 progenitors, suggesting that it corresponds to rX, while HB.3 appears to correspond to the r4 segment, and HB.1 to the r2 + r3 segment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the PHPD analysis.

claim: HB.1 appears to correspond to the r2 + r3 segment.
source: The HB.2 population contains r5 + r6 progenitors, suggesting that it corresponds to rX, while HB.3 appears to correspond to the r4 segment, and HB.1 to the r2 + r3 segment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the PHPD analysis.

claim: The HB.1 cluster expresses markers of both r2 (vgll3) and r3 (egr2b, nab1b) at 10hpf.
source: Our data reveal that the HB.1 cluster expresses markers of both r2 (vgll3) and r3 (egr2b, nab1b) at 10hpf (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 3.

claim: Individual HB.1 cells co-express r2 and r3 markers and such co-expression was confirmed by HCR analyses in developing embryos.
source: A closer examination further demonstrated that individual HB.1 cells co-express r2 and r3 markers and such co-expression was confirmed by HCR analyses in developing embryos (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 6.

claim: HB.1 cells possess a mixed gene expression profile and may be able to take on both r2 and r3 fates.
source: These findings indicate that HB.1 cells possess a mixed gene expression profile and may be able to take on both r2 and r3 fates.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the co-expression data.

claim: When 10hpf cells are computationally integrated with cells from 13hpf and 16hpf, they contribute to both the r2 and r3 clusters.
source: Accordingly, when 10hpf cells are computationally integrated with cells from 13hpf and 16hpf, they contribute to both the r2 and r3 clusters (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 6.

claim: The gene expression profiles of HB.1–3 cells are distinct from those of their corresponding rhombomere derivatives.
source: Notably, the gene expression profiles of HB.1–3 cells are distinct from those of their corresponding rhombomere derivatives and our comparisons between developmental timepoints identified a profound change in gene expression as PHPD cells transition to rhombomere cells (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Comparisons between developmental timepoints identified a profound change in gene expression as PHPD cells transition to rhombomere cells.
source: Notably, the gene expression profiles of HB.1–3 cells are distinct from those of their corresponding rhombomere derivatives and our comparisons between developmental timepoints identified a profound change in gene expression as PHPD cells transition to rhombomere cells (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mixed gene expression profiles are resolved during rhombomere formation.
source: This indicates that the mixed gene expression profiles are resolved during rhombomere formation (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 8 showing a model.

claim: TFs expressed in the PHPDs may repress each other to drive distinct rhombomere fates.
source: Analogous to dorsoventral patterning of the neural tube by repressive interactions between TFs (Briscoe and Novitch, 2008; Kutejova et al., 2016), we hypothesize that TFs expressed in the PHPDs repress each other to drive distinct rhombomere fates.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis with citations to analogous processes.

claim: vgll3 and egr2b (or components of their respective GRNs) may repress each other's transcription in HB.1 to force an r2 versus an r3 fate.
